draft.title: Graphing parabolas
card: The graph of y = x² is a U-shaped curve called a parabola. To draw it, work out y for several x-values, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve.
Example: x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 give y = 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. Squaring a negative number gives a positive answer, so y is never below 0.
The turning point is where the curve changes direction. For y = x² it is at the origin (0, 0), the lowest point.
The y-axis is the line of symmetry. The left side is a mirror image of the right side, so (3, 9) and (−3, 9) are both on the curve.
draft.remember: y = x² is a U-shaped parabola, with its turning point at (0, 0) and a mirror line along the y-axis.

a.q: Which point lies on the graph of y = x²?
a.why: When x = −4, y = (−4)² = 16, because a negative number squared is positive. (4, 8) is tempting, but it comes from doubling 4 instead of squaring it.

b.q: The point (5, 25) is on the graph of y = x². Which other point must also be on the graph?
b.why: The y-axis is the line of symmetry, so the point (5, 25) has a mirror image at (−5, 25). Changing the sign of y, as in (−5, −25), would put the point below the x-axis, but the curve never goes below it.
b.clue: Reflect the point across the y-axis.

problems.detail: The why describes (−5, −25) as 'changing the sign of y', but that option changes the sign of both x and y. It should say something like 'changing the signs of both x and y'.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct, and each question has a single right answer. The only fix is in the explanation for question b, which says (−5, −25) changes only the sign of y when it changes both signs.
